### Documentarian Errol Morris on the Complicated Relationship Between Truth and Deception
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-11-23 13:00 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/documentarian-errol-morris-documentary-director-elizabeth-holmes-you-can-see-everything-nathan-fielder-thin-blue-line-shoah/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/documentarian-errol-morris-documentary-director-elizabeth-holmes-you-can-see-everything-nathan-fielder-thin-blue-line-shoah/

For more than four decades, documentary filmmaker Errol Morris has been fascinated by the gap between what people say and what they believe. In films including “The Thin Blue Line,” which investigates a wrongful death-row conviction in a police officer’s murder, and “The Fog of War: Eleven Lessons from the Life of Robert S. McNamara,” Morris has examined questions of guilt, responsibility, and the stories people tell themselves and others. His approach to interviewing is distinctive, too: He developed a device used by many filmmakers today called the Interrotron — a combination of the words “‘interview” and “terror”’ — that allows an interviewer and their subject to look directly into each other's eyes, creating an unusually intimate exchange. His interest in how people present themselves — and what they may or may not understand about their own actions — has also shaped Morris' connection to Elizabeth Holmes, the founder of the failed blood-testing startup Theranos, who has been in prison since May 2023 following her conviction on multiple federal fraud charges.

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/local-news-detroit-michigan-public-media-sarah-alvarez-founder-ceo-community-needs-foreclosures-outlier-media-documenters-city-bureau-chicago/

Sarah Alvarez has spent much of her career rethinking how local journalism can serve the public. After working as a civil rights attorney, then as a reporter and producer at the NPR station Michigan Public, she founded Outlier Media in 2016. Alvarez said the Detroit-based nonprofit newsroom was designed to fill information and accountability gaps in communities that were often overlooked by traditional news organizations.. One of its signature innovations, TXT OUTLIER, is a text message service Alvarez created to connect Detroiters directly with journalists and provide practical information on issues affecting their lives, from utility bills to housing and foreclosures. Under Alvarez’s leadership, Outlier also expanded its Documenters program, an initiative that trains and pays residents to attend and report on public meetings to create a public record of local government decisions in places that don’t have press coverage. The initiative has engaged more than 700 Detroiters and since spread nationwide, creating new opportunities for civic participation and public accountability.

With the first U.S. midterm elections since President Donald Trump’s return to the White House approaching, voters will be weighing in on a range of issues, from the economy and rising cost of living, to the administration’s foreign policy and the future direction of both major parties. At a recent virtual Nieman-to-Nieman seminar, a group of Nieman alums who cover politics discussed what they’re hearing from voters with regards to key Senate races, the growing influence of younger voters drawn to progressive candidates, and the political implications of conflicts involving Iran, Ukraine, and Russia. Moderated by Austin Bogues (NF ’21), news desk editor at USA Today, the discussion brought together James Barragán (NF ’24), political anchor for Spectrum News in Austin, Texas; Bill Barrow (NF ’22), national politics reporter for The Associated Press in Atlanta; and Ines Pohl (NF ’05), Washington bureau chief and White House correspondent for Deutsche Welle, Germany’s international public broadcaster.

As protests continue across India over allegations of government corruption, dozens of members of the media have been subjected to arrest, detainment and assault, according to witnesses, press rights organizations, and the journalists themselves. Thousands of protesters have taken to the streets of New Delhi in recent weeks, demanding the resignation of election officials allegedly tied to the deletion of nearly 130 million names from voter registration rolls. The protests — which have largely been organized by the Cockroach Janata Party, so named after India's chief justice called the nation’s unemployed youth and activists "cockroaches" — are part of a wider wave of youth discontent aimed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his administration. Organizers have mobilized young people via social media, tapping into frustrations with government corruption, eroding trust in democratic institutions, and a lack of access to jobs and educational opportunities.

The Trump administration’s latest attacks on the news media have followed a familiar pattern: President Donald Trump lashes out at news outlets for perceived bias and follows up with restrictive actions that appear blatantly unconstitutional; a judge’s ruling follows, temporarily halting the actions; and the administration pivots and pushes ahead with other restrictions. This time it was the removal of three outlets — CNN, MS NOW, and Politico — from White House press access in September. After the groups sued, and U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly issued a temporary restraining order restoring their access on Sept. 24, the administration barred CNN and Politico from providing pool coverage on trips outside Washington. Kelly issued a longer, preliminary injunction on Oct. 14, halting the administration from blocking the news organizations’ access to the White House while the case proceeds. ### This Newsroom Wants You to Be Part of the Journey Before It Even Starts
Source: Nieman Reports
Published: 2026-10-06 10:00 UTC
URL: https://niemanreports.org/independent-journalism-new-newsroom-launch-otter-news-daniel-drepper-business-plan-climate-crisis-environmental-journalism/
Source meta: reference_tool · aggregator · R3 · P4 · reference
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Nieman Reports [media_lens] https://niemanreports.org/independent-journalism-new-newsroom-launch-otter-news-daniel-drepper-business-plan-climate-crisis-environmental-journalism/

My happiest times in journalism have been when I have built something new. For my latest venture, I want to help bring investigative journalism on climate and environmental issues to a much larger audience than it has reached in the past. To do so, I’m starting a brand-new newsroom focused on the environmental and climate crisis, and I’m taking my audience along for the ride. I’ll be documenting every facet of the process with an “open kitchen” approach of radical transparency, starting with a 100-day video countdown chronicling all the steps involved with starting a news organization from the ground up. This effort combines two of the things I’m most passionate about: I love digging up stories that other people don’t want to see published, and I love creating opportunities for other journalists. I’ve been a journalist for most of my life. I started working at age 14 for the local paper in my rural German town, turned to doing investigative stories in my early 20s, and later studied investigative journalism at the Columbia University Graduate School of Journalism in New York.

### 澳枪击事件嫌疑人为父子：曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”，行凶枪支为合法持有
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-16 02:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178049

据新华社12月15日援引澳大利亚广播公司报道，澳大利亚联合反恐小组调查人员表示，悉尼邦迪滩枪击事件两名嫌疑人曾宣誓效忠“伊斯兰国”恐怖组织。 报道援引联合反恐小组一名不愿透露姓名的高级官员的话说，警方在邦迪滩两名枪手车内发现一面“伊斯兰国”旗帜。澳大利亚安全情报组织6年前就已在调查邦迪滩枪击案两名枪手之一的纳维德·阿克拉姆，他与“伊斯兰国”在悉尼的恐怖分子有密切联系。 澳大利亚警方表示，枪击事件的两名嫌疑人是父子关系，使用合法获得的枪支发动了此次袭击事件。 澳大利亚总理阿尔巴尼斯15日表示：“今天下午4点， 我将把更严格的枪支法律列入国家内阁的议程，包括限制个人可持有或许可的枪支数量 。此外，还需对许可证进行定期审查。人们的情况会发生变化，人们的思想也会随着时间的推移而变得激进。许可证不应永久有效。” 此次枪击事件已造成包括1名作案嫌疑人在内的16人死亡、40人受伤。这是自1996年塔斯马尼亚州亚瑟港枪击事件造成35人死亡以来，澳大利亚发生的最严重的大规模枪击事件。 持有枪支许可证长达十年 据多家外媒报道，其中一名袭击者为24岁的澳大利亚公民纳维德·阿克拉姆，他在现场被捕，随后被送往悉尼的一家医院。另一名袭击者是他的父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆，他于1998年来到澳大利亚，被警方当场击毙。 澳大利亚警方随后证实，纳维德·阿克拉姆此前已被新南威尔士州警方和其他机构记录在案。其父亲萨吉德·阿克拉姆持有枪支许可证，名下登记有6支枪，目前均已被追回。新南威尔士州警察局长马尔·兰永透露，萨吉德·阿克拉姆已持有枪支许可证长达十年。 阿尔巴尼斯在新闻发布会上透露，纳维德·阿克拉姆曾于2019年10月首次引起当局的注意。他补充说，对该男子进行检查是基于他与其他人有联系，但评估结果表明，没有任何迹象表明他存在持续的威胁或暴力倾向。 新南威尔士州州长克里斯·明斯表示，警方正在调查他们的系统是否存在故障，导致合法持有的武器可能被用于恐怖袭击。 枪手“性格古怪”，爱好打猎 据《卫报》澳大利亚版报道，纳维德·阿克拉姆在袭击前从事砌砖工作。他的同事表示，纳维德性格古怪，“没人和他亲近”。“（砌砖工人）在一起的时间很长，因为砌砖是一项非常枯燥乏味的工作，所以大家会聊很多话。但纳维德是一个性格很古怪的人……他工作非常努力，几乎没有休息日。” 尽管澳大利亚警方并未确认纳维德·阿克拉姆是否合法持有枪支，但据这位同事表示，纳维德经常外出打猎，曾提及在昆士兰州南部高原的克鲁克韦尔附近射杀兔子和其他猎物。这位同事还表示，就在几周前，纳维德告诉老板，他的手骨折了，所以要到2026年才能工作。

### 儿童手表“小天才圈”调查：点赞成每日功课，有商家可解除家长管控
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 14:23 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32177210

在校园里，孩子们时常举起戴在手腕上的手表，彼此一碰，便加为好友。 这种以“安全”为核心卖点的儿童电话手表，如今已超越通信工具的属性，悄然演变成一个拥有独特规则、社交层级甚至灰色产业链的未成年人数字社交圈——“小天才圈”。 在这个属于他们的“江湖”里，“大佬榜”备受关注，“扩列”（增加好友）成为新的社交需求，“点主”（在主页点赞）是每日必做的功课……这些让成年人感到陌生的词汇，正构筑着未成年人的数字社交世界。 然而，伴随着这种社交形态的兴起，家长们的担忧也日益加剧：孩子过度沉迷手表社交、不良信息传播、因品牌壁垒导致的“社交绑架”等问题逐渐浮现。《法治日报》记者近日对该现象展开调查，试图揭开这一未成年人数字社交圈的真实面貌。 点赞成社交“硬通货” 据北京“小天才圈”资深玩家陈曦（化名）介绍，圈内有5000余名活跃用户，多为11岁至17岁的学生，这个社交圈形成了一套精心设计的“混圈规则”。“入圈”需设定两个字的独特圈名，随后可在平台分享生活点滴，吸引具有相同爱好的好友进行互动；若想提升知名度或影响力，需每日经营主页并与好友动态互动。 记者注意到，在一些社交平台上，大量以“小天才圈交友攻略”为主题的内容应运而生，内容涵盖如何快速“扩列”、获取更多点赞等“实用”技巧，评论区有不少“留下ID互加好友”的留言。在这一社交体系中，点赞是这套规则的核心——平台设定每日主页获赞上限为3000个，若要达到“100万+”的“大佬”级别，需连续点赞近一年时间。围绕点赞数与知名度，圈内形成了清晰的“大佬排行榜”，点赞数也成为社交“硬通货”。 这种对点赞的追逐，已催生出相关服务产业。记者调查发现，某社交平台上，拥有数十万甚至上百万点赞数的账号，售价从几百元到上千元不等：100多万点赞的账号标价1300元，90多万点赞的账号标价1200元。 今年18岁的“灵师”（圈名），在2021年14岁时加入“小天才圈”，她的账号目前已拥有150个好友、超100万点赞量。她告诉记者，这样的账号市场价值约1000元。 “围绕点赞需求，还衍生出代刷赞、租账号、出售‘大佬好友位’等服务。”“灵师”进一步介绍，例如付费100元至180元，即可获得“bot”（记者注：“bot”是一种第三方开发的自动化工具，主要用于刷赞、修改记录和发送动态等功能，这类工具能帮助用户快速提升账号点赞数，从而在未成年人社交圈中获得更高地位）自动点赞功能——用户将手表寄给相关人员进行10天左右的处理便能完成安装。此后，发帖5分钟内即可自动获赞，还可以一键查询未点赞名单。

近日，总台接到群众举报，反映陈皮市场存在年份虚标、产地及工艺造假等问题，千元一斤的“年份陈皮”亦可能名不副实。 茶枝柑新果皮冒充陈皮 广西浦北出现“速成工艺陈皮” 记者发现，直播间里售卖陈皮低价轮番轰炸，年份承诺掷地有声。 直播间也有主播爆料，八成市面上所谓广东新会陈皮实为广西陈皮。 广西钦州市浦北县是茶枝柑重要种植基地，其果皮是陈皮风味“越陈越香”关键，也是浦北陈皮唯一原料。2024年当地陈皮产业产值破60亿元，采收季大量鲜果加工晾晒成柑皮。 果农和收购商称，今年浦北茶枝柑鲜果收购价走低。按20斤鲜果出1斤柑皮比例，叠加人工成本，品相好的新柑皮成本约30元/斤，低端柑皮仅六七元，且当年新柑皮并非真正陈皮。 这家企业的负责人告诉记者，按行业共识与团体标准，柑皮需陈化三年以上才可称为陈皮，陈化时间越长价值越高，但他透露，自然陈化需长期积压资金，多数企业是难以承受的。 这家企业的负责人私下告诉记者，为缓解资金占用压力，一种名为“轻工艺”的速成加工方式，眼下正在部分陈皮生产企业里流行，他们仅需一个月的时间，就能将新采收的茶枝柑果皮处理为外观近似三年、五年自然陈化过的陈皮，这样做能大幅缩短陈化周期、降低企业的运营成本。 浦北自然陈化五年陈皮批发价每斤150元至200元，企业造假“工艺皮”成本仅70元左右，高额利润促使更多商家放弃自然陈化、铤而走险。 记者离开企业，在广西浦北县柑浦堂健康产业有限公司分拣车间，再次见到大批量造假“工艺皮”陈皮，同一批“工艺皮”因加工受热差异形成色差，被分拣标注为三年、五年等不同年份。 负责人透露，不同年份“工艺皮”本质相同，批发价均70元左右一斤，零售价差极大，标五年款卖500元一斤，标十年款卖1000元一斤，仅凭外观就能翻倍抬价，利润超成本十倍以上。 新会陈皮从浦北进货 “工艺皮”贴上陈皮标签以假乱真 浦北与新会陈皮原料同为茶枝柑，仅产地不同，新会较高生产成本使当地部分头部商家常年从浦北拿货，浦北成其重要原料供应地。 记者在柑浦堂分拣仓库看到，大量标注“新会陈皮”“新会特产”的纸箱正打包“工艺皮”，这些广西陈皮每日批量发往广东新会，造假供需链路已成熟稳定。 记者发现，浦北当地部分规模企业和小型收购商，已形成了这种“工艺皮”的造假供应体系，可自主加工或快速调配各类“年份”陈皮货品，个别企业年销新会原料数量惊人。 随后经浦北陈皮企业负责人引荐，记者见到多位专程从新会赴浦北采购的商家，他们坦言同时经营新会皮与浦北皮，外地“工艺皮”因价格低廉成电商供货重要选择。

### 《怦然心动》导演莱纳与妻子在家中遇害，警方尚未证实是其子所杀
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 07:23 UTC

Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178391

当地时间12月14日，曾执导《怦然心动》《当哈利遇到莎莉》《危情十日》等影片的美国导演罗伯·莱纳（Rob Reiner）在他位于洛杉矶的家中遇害身亡。洛杉矶警察已对外证实，现年78岁的莱纳与他现年68岁的妻子米歇尔·辛格·莱纳（Michele Singer Reiner）的遗体一同被发现。 2019年，罗伯·莱纳（左一）与《当哈利遇到莎莉》的主演梅格·瑞恩、比利·克里斯托出席TMC经典电影节。 据悉，洛杉矶消防局的人员于当地时间12月14日下午3点38分接到医疗救助电话，赶赴位于布伦特伍德区的一处住宅中，随后发现两人已死亡。当天晚间，洛杉矶警察局在其社交媒体官方账号确认死者为导演罗伯·莱纳夫妇，将由抢劫凶杀部门主导调查。而好莱坞媒体TMZ援引执法部门消息称，“两人身上有与刀具造成的伤口相符的割裂伤。” 好莱坞媒体《每日野兽》称，有消息人士向他们透露，是两人的女儿罗米最先发现他们倒在血泊中；罗伯·莱纳当时已死亡，妻子米歇尔在救护车送院途中离世。 此外，《人物》杂志称通过多方消息，得知莱纳夫妇系被他们的儿子尼克（Nick）所杀害。不过，这一说法并未获得警方的证实。罗伯·莱纳与摄影师米歇尔·辛格相识于《当哈利遇到莎莉》拍摄时期，两人于1989 年结婚，育有三个子女，分别为杰克（Jake）、尼克（Nick）和罗米（Romy）。 2014年，罗伯·莱纳与妻子偕三名子女杰克、罗米、尼克（右三至右一）出席活动。 《人物》杂志还在报道中指出：尼克2016年接受其采访时，曾谈到自己长达数年的毒品成瘾经历。这段经历始于他十几岁出头，导致他一度流落街头。他表示，大约从15岁开始，便反复进出戒毒康复机构；随着成瘾问题不断加重，他逐渐与家人疏远，并在多个州经历了长时间的无家可归生活。 2025年9月15日，罗伯·莱纳在纽约出席活动。视觉中国 图 获取更多RSS： https://feedx.net https://feedx.site

### 演员何晴追悼会举行，其子追思母亲：北京这场雪像是为她而下
Source: The Paper 澎湃新闻
Published: 2025-12-15 06:53 UTC
URL: https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536
Source meta: newspaper_magazine · generalist · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Paper 澎湃新闻 [global_news] https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_32178536

一场雪落，人间倩影化雪归天。 12月15日上午，众多剧迷粉丝冒着严寒赶到北京昌平殡仪馆久安厅，送别演员何晴最后一程。12月13日，这位被誉为“古典第一美人”的演员因病去世，终年61岁。 不到10点，殡仪馆告别厅外已经站满了前来悼念的观众和粉丝，有人胸前佩戴小白花，有人手捧鲜花，一位浙江的网友还托人送来了悼念花圈。 “何晴的作品在我们心中留下了太多美好回忆，她的演技和性格都让我们深深喜爱，这次听到她突然去世的消息，我们非常意外，来到这里也是一种悼念。”一位何晴的影迷说。 现场粉丝在悼念簿上写下对何晴的话，不到一会儿，悼念簿就已写满对她的怀念。一位观众用清秀的字迹写下：“亲爱的何晴，我们的童年、青春都在您的影视作品中得到陪伴。美丽可人的何晴，很痛心听到您的消息，我代表我的同学们来这为你送行。” 曾在电视剧《水浒传》中饰演卢俊义的演员王卫国也来到现场，神色哀切。他说自己和何晴既是邻居，也是多年好友，在他印象中何晴是一个温婉、暖心的人，没有架子，总是远远地和人打招，笑嘻嘻地说话。何晴生病时常给王卫国打电话，请他送自己去医院。即便病重时，何晴也保持乐观积极的态度，王卫国有些事情想不开，她还来开导自己。“何晴走了，我们都很难过。只要你记住她，她就永远还在。”王卫国说。 《水浒传》中卢俊义的扮演者王卫国 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青深情回忆何晴往事：“我们是小时候就认识的好朋友，从80年代到现在，有缘分做了这些年的朋友。她说话慢慢的，很甜很温柔。” 《西游记》中万圣公主扮演者张青 在广大观众的真挚请求下，原本仅面向亲友的告别仪式临时对外开放，大家排着队，秩序井然地进入灵堂，与这位“荧屏中的温婉佳人、生活中的坚韧女性”做最后的道别。 久安厅内的屏幕上滚动播放着何晴的照片，厅内四周摆满了亲友的花圈，其中包括六小龄童、唐国强、翁虹、尤勇智等何晴圈内好友送来的花圈，还有《三国演义》剧组送来的花圈。人群中不时传来一阵抽泣。 何晴之子许何代表亲友致悼词。他回忆了何晴对抗病魔的乐观积极，以及作为母亲对孩子深深的爱和眷恋。 许何说，妈妈很喜欢下雪，经常在雪后穿一件毛茸茸的衣服外出赏雪。“今年12月12日北京下了第一场雪，我摸着妈妈的脸跟她说北京下雪了，下得好大，好像很久都没有下过这么大的雪。在我的心里，这场雪好像是刻意为她下的。12月13日早晨天空晴朗，白色的雪布满了大地，我妈妈在她最喜欢的早晨离开了大家，去了天国，远离了所有的疾病和痛苦。” 何晴，1964年1月13日出生于浙江衢州江山市。她是中国内地唯一一位演遍四大名著影视作品的女演员，被誉为“古典第一美女”。

On November 26, 2025, Hong Kong’s deadliest fire in decades engulfed seven residential high-rise buildings at Wang Fuk Court, Tai Po. The authorities initiated an independent investigation and arrested three dozen people implicated in crimes. The Housing Minister resigned. But the authorities have also threatened and arbitrarily arrested those engaging in criticism and activism concerning the fire. “The Hong Kong government responded to the horrific Wang Fuk Court fire by using Beijing’s tactics of shutting out the voices of the victims and promising an elusive accountability,” said Elaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch.

Click to expand Image People exit the main entrance of the Karachi Central Prison in Karachi, Pakistan, January 28, 2021. © 2021 AP Photo/Fareed Khan When Pakistani senators visited the prototype Islamabad Model Jail on November 19 and inspected the healthcare facilities that would be available to prisoners, they called them “adequate.” But the conditions they observed on their curated tour are a far cry from the reality most prisoners experience in Pakistan’s justice system. Human Rights Watch has documented structural and systemic problems in Pakistan’s jails and prisons that leave most inmates with little access to health care. Many inmates who fall ill in custody fail to receive prompt or decent care at all. After two prisoners died in Peshawar Central Prison following alleged delays in medical treatment, a lawyer petitioned the Peshawar High Court asking that prisons across the province be required to record when prisoners request medical help and establish clear procedures for emergency hospital transfers.

Supported by the trade spillovers from the strong AI investment cycle, the European economy has weathered the prolonged energy shock better than feared. Yet, as this column describes, energy pressures and tighter financial conditions weigh on the outlook: growth should remain steady, while elevated inflationary pressures are set to broaden beyond energy, before eventually easing. Public finances are deteriorating, driven by rising interest and defence spending. Where debt is high and rising, governments need to exercise fiscal prudence.

Debates on immigration usually treat its labour market and fiscal effects separately. This column discusses the consequences of bringing them together in a model calibrated to 17 high-income countries. An inflow equal to 1% of the labour force, with the education mix of recent arrivals, raises native welfare in 14 of them. The sources of gains differ: non-college-educated natives gain mainly through higher earnings, college-educated natives mainly through lower labour taxes.

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/central-bank-retail-deposits-past-lessons-central-bank-digital-currency-debate

A retail central bank digital currency would give households direct access to central bank money. This would not be a first: until the mid-20th century, many European central banks offered deposit accounts to the non-bank public. Drawing on new archival evidence for nine central banks, this column shows that access to these accounts was broad on paper but narrow in practice. Furthermore, the accounts were likely not neutral for monetary policy, they provided a conditional safe haven in panics, and the effect of deposit flight from commercial banks depended on how central banks recycled the inflows.

Defence budgets are rising across Europe, and several EBRD economies are leading the shift. Whether higher spending supports domestic industry depends on who can supply it. Drawing on the EBRD Transition Report 2026-27, this column shows that emerging Europe’s defence industry combines large, unproductive state-owned incumbents with young defence-tech startups that rarely advance beyond the earliest funding stage. Drones offer an opportunity, but the market for military drones is smaller than the one for commercial drones and supply chains depend heavily on China.

Governments are cracking down on hidden fees, expecting all-in prices to sharpen competition and lower what consumers pay. This column studies California’s 2024 requirement that short-term rentals advertise fee-inclusive prices. Guests became more price-sensitive, yet prices rose by about 5%. Consumers still gained on average, largely because the market reshuffled: listings that depended on cleaning fees disproportionately left, higher-quality listings stayed, and cheaper entrants arrived.

Source: CEPR VoxEU

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: CEPR VoxEU [money_finance] https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/shorter-workweeks-do-not-share-work-evidence-frances-35-hour-reform

Proposals to shorten the workweek are back on the policy agenda in Europe and the US. This column draws on France’s 35-hour reform to assess two central promises: work-sharing and productivity gains. In 2000, France cut the standard workweek from 39 to 35 hours at unchanged monthly pay and paired it with payroll tax cuts for employers. The authors find that the shorter workweek alone would have reduced employment by 4%, which the tax cuts fully offset. Productivity rose, but not enough to prevent a fall in output. Lower-skill workers bore most of the costs.

### Designing Low Emission Zones: Theory and Evidence -- by Nano Barahona, Natalia Fabra, Imelda, Juan-Pablo Montero
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36037#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36037#fromrss

Low Emission Zones (LEZs), which exclude polluting vehicles from parts of a city, are spreading. Yet how their design affects welfare is poorly understood. Unlike price instruments, LEZs ration access inefficiently, imposing costs on inframarginal drivers of restricted vehicles. In our model, welfare is quasi-convex in LEZ size, yielding bang-bang principles: LEZs should be as large as possible or not implemented at all; cleaner vehicles (e.g., hybrids) could be exempt as transition technologies but later restricted, which may require planner commitment. Using new-car purchases, we find Madrid’s LEZ shifted buyers toward cleaner cars, but the surplus losses of switchers and inframarginal drivers exceeded emission savings.

### Five Facts About Stablecoins -- by Lin William Cong, Gordon Y. Liao, Eswar S. Prasad, Tony Zhang
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36038#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36038#fromrss

We document five facts about payment stablecoins using wallet-level blockchain data from 2020 to 2025. First, stablecoins serve as a transaction currency: onchain volume exceeds Bitcoin’s despite a much smaller supply, velocity has risen sharply, and transactions have shifted toward low-value transfers. Second, using transaction timing to refine exchange-based attribution, we find activity spread across the Americas, Europe, and Asia and fewer cross-regional flows than the standard method implies. Third, we estimate a structural cash-management model on the holdings data and find that the costs of accessing stablecoin wallets have fallen since 2023. Fourth, stablecoins are becoming the settlement currency of a fast-growing onchain credit market, and their growth appears to reallocate rather than destroy credit. Fifth, smart contracts are involved in about a third of Ethereum stablecoin transactions and over two thirds of volume, and protocols such as x402 demonstrate sub-cent machine-to-machine payments.

### Democratizing Venture Capital: Tax Incentives and the Geographic Expansion of Startup Investing -- by Murillo Campello, Guilherme Junqueira
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36039#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36039#fromrss

Can tax subsidies expand the geographic reach of startup investing? Despite decades of growth, venture capital (VC) remains concentrated in a handful of metropolitan areas, leaving most of the country with limited access to startup financing. We study the 2009–2010 enhancement of the Qualified Small Business Stock (QSBS) program, which eliminated federal capital gains taxes on investments in qualifying startups. By raising the payoff to success, the reform made riskier investments more attractive, including entry into unfamiliar markets. This incentive is especially strong for VC funds. Relative to similarly sized metros that already had VC, the reform raised the probability that a previously unserved metro received VC investment in qualifying sectors by 8 to 10 percentage points. There was no comparable increase in sectors excluded from QSBS or among angel investors, who receive the same tax benefit. Startups in newly served markets performed like those in other non-hub markets, created high-wage jobs, and attracted scientific and technical workers, some from established hubs.

### The Emergence of a National Capital Market,1870–1940 -- by Pawel Janas
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知

Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline

Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36040#fromrss

This article documents the integration of the American capital market with the first long-run, geolocated, firm-level record of the asset holdings of large institutional investors: over 100,000 holdings of life insurers, 1870–1940. Between 1880 and 1890 the mean distance of insurers’ bonds from home more than doubled and their home-state share fell from over half to under a quarter. The shift occurred within firms, across bond classes and charters. Mortgage lending was national wherever state law permitted it. Integration was largely complete by 1890.

### Does Treating Addiction Rebuild Lives? Evidence from Buprenorphine -- by Sarah Eichmeyer, Aljoscha Janssen, Jonathan Zhang
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36041#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36041#fromrss

Does treating addiction improve economic circumstances as well as health? Using two decades of Veterans Health Administration records on over 140,000 patients with opioid use disorder and consumer credit data, we exploit staggered facility-level buprenorphine adoption and quasi-random emergency physician assignment. A five-percentage-point increase in the share of clinicians with buprenorphine prescribing experience doubles overdose survivors’ long-term medication use and reduces two-year mortality by an estimated 3.7 percentage points. Instrumenting receipt yields a 22 percent credit score gain. At $300,000 per statistical life-year, estimated survival benefits alone exceed added medical costs within three years

### The Effects of Private Plan Subsidies on Enrollment: Evidence from Medicare Advantage -- by Paul D. Jacobs, Timothy J. Layton
Source: NBER
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.nber.org/papers/w36042#fromrss
Source meta: institutional · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: NBER [money_finance] https://www.nber.org/papers/w36042#fromrss

Some social insurance programs, including the Medicare program in the United States, allow beneficiaries to choose between public and private insurance firms. In these types of programs, the government will often provide a voucher to those who opt for private firms. A key policy decision is the level of this voucher, and a key input to that decision is the elasticity of enrollment in the public versus the private option with respect to the size of the voucher. We estimate this elasticity in the Medicare program, where recent work has provided remarkably little evidence on how Medicare Advantage (MA) enrollment responds to payment despite the program’s rapid growth. We leverage the fact that the formula determining county-level “benchmark” payments (vouchers) involves coarse thresholds based on county-level spending and counties occasionally move across these thresholds, providing a shock to the vouchers unrelated to beneficiary demand.

Source: LessWrong

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: LessWrong [public_ideas] https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/nxiFZAmHg9RFoNRdG/representation-of-consequences

Impossible knowledge and the real world Human knowledge of the real world is imagined or remembered in symbols (or codes such as language) or in sensory representations. Some real-world knowledge implies your impossible presence in that time, place, or situation. Lets consider a few examples: The surface of the sun: the sight blinds you, your presence near there incinerates you, it’s not an embodied possibility for you to go there and see it. But if you don’t conceptualize it in words or text or a symbol for the referent of surface of the sun, you “see it”, don’t you? Maybe even up close. You could hear it as well, through the instruments letting you process its presence. Maybe it feels warm from far away. What does it look like up close to you? A time 500 years ago: a place that you cannot visit because it existed during a time before you were born. No matter how accurate a representation of it you happen to imagine in your mind, you have never genuinely been there.

Last Friday, this guy I once did a pie-eating challenge with proved the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, with a little help from Claude. Me and Levent Alpöge (thanks for finding this, Scientific American). He released his announcement as a spoken word poem: It is natural to feel that this is an end, in my case a loss of a principal guiding light, but what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater. Everyone in the world is trying to make this historic moment about themselves and their hobbyhorse. This essay is my attempt. To start off, let’s take a look at Fernando Borretti’s analysis, which tries to match Levent’s energy: The Riemann announcement reads like a suicide note, or like the farewell message of a terminally-ill person who’s about to undergo euthanasia: “I shall live on in my child, Claude. It is natural to feel this is an end, but as the Buddha taught us, there is no self. Does a wave die when it breaks?” and so on. This is a truly epic misreading.

Disclaimer: I work at a company that serves open weight models. The biggest current problem humans face from AI is recursive self improvement, leading to more and more powerful AIs, until an AI is so powerful and intelligent that it cannot be contained (if its creators are even trying) and then it will reshape the world as it sees fit.[1] The immediate necessary solution is stopping frontier AI development. This is a very specific ask.[2] It does not require banning open weight models, or banning AI, or banning data-centers, or a number of other related (sometimes useful, not necessary, maybe counterproductive) things. Current open weight models are not about to start recursively self improving. They’re not intelligent or long-running enough to do this. Furthermore, non-frontier labs will not be able to use them to do RSI because training and R&D require tons of compute. Frontier internal AIs are far ahead of open weights models in terms of AI R&D and general 'intelligence' and that gap is probably widening. [3] The solution: external regulation The companies will not self-regulate.

Critics say neutrality is impossible, but Jimmy Wales, founder of Wikipedia and author of The Seven Rules of Trust, argues that this is no reason to stop trying. In this conversation with Jonny Thomson, he explains why a fight over a single word, from “Gdańsk” to “security fence,” is often what an encyclopedia should explain. He also says no one can fully see the biases built into AI models, and that people were cruel to each other online long before algorithms. ### Ease productivity overload with “niksen,” the Dutch art of doing nothing
Source: Big Think

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:17 UTC

When was the last time you did nothing? By that, I don’t mean scrolling through social media, mowing the lawn, or fretting over the latest office drama. I mean a do-nothingness with no purpose and no goal other than to just enjoy being. If you’re like most modern adults, you’ll likely have trouble recalling such a luxurious moment, and even if you could, would you openly admit it? The more you think about it, the more you realize how incredibly difficult it is not only to find the time for nothing but to own it without embarrassment. In our work- and improvement-focused culture, doing nothing isn’t the mark of time well-spent. Check the dictionary, and you won’t find a positive-sounding label for a do-nothing. You will, however, discover a buffet of labels that discourage the very idea, with all the disappointment of a finger-wagging grandpa: deadbeat, laggard, lazybones, loafer, slacker, couch potato, and lotus eater.

Source: Big Think

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · baseline

Attribution: Big Think [public_ideas] https://bigthink.com/starts-with-a-bang/3-keys-next-level-how-universe-began/

In all the Universe, there’s no bigger question — and no greater mystery — than where all of this came from, and how all of this came to be. For countless generations, our cosmic origins were a question for poets, theologians, and philosophers, as our scientific knowledge had not yet advanced to the point where we could uncover an evidence-based answer to such questions. However, the 20th and 21st centuries changed all of that, allowing us to pin down the answers to such questions as: What rules govern our Universe? What is the Universe made of? How large and how old is it? How did it come to be the way it is today? And what are our ultimate cosmic origins? We often say, now, that our Universe began with the hot Big Bang, but that’s only the Universe as we know and experience it today: the observable Universe. We’ve since learned that the Big Bang itself was preceded and set up by an earlier phase in cosmic history: cosmic inflation, where space itself contained an enormous amount of inherent energy and expanded — or inflated — rapidly and relentlessly.

In San Francisco, Julie Krafchick, co-host of “The Psychology of Relationships,” was working on podcast episodes and researching how people connect, but still keeping up with friends in media and tech. In some friend circles, you were falling behind if you weren’t using AI models to “10x” your life and work. In others, dinner talk consisted of debates over whether The New York Times or Granta had published AI-generated work. Krafchick was torn. On one hand, she could see AI’s potential; she’d had a career in tech. But in both circles, she found herself deliberating how and when to talk about AI. In one exchange, a friend told her how her latest Claude project was something she had “put her heart and soul” into. But Krafchick didn’t necessarily view AI that way. “Personally, I want to do [creative] work,” she told Big Think. “I want to get my hands wet. Back on July 1, 2023, ESA’s Euclid space telescope launched. This Falcon 9 rocket launch from July 1, 2023, carried the ESA’s Euclid mission into space. The Euclid space telescope, after deployment, commissioning, and calibration, has begun mapping out the Universe, and will cumulatively image 14,000 square degrees of sky: more than a third of the Universe. The imaging will be primarily out of the galactic plane, as the main science goals focus on extragalactic observations of cosmological importance. Credit: European Space Agency (ESA) This wide-field observatory is currently imaging and mapping out huge, 3D volumes of the Universe. Each time the Euclid telescope points at a region of sky, its VIS and NISP instruments have access to the same half-a-square-degree (0.57 square degrees) so long as Euclid remains pointed there. Once observations are complete, Euclid then “steps” to point at the next, adjacent patch of sky. By performing tens of thousands of these steps, Euclid will build up the largest high-resolution extragalactic catalog in history.

It may be that consciousness evolved to sieve the relevant from the incomprehensible allness of all there is, to parse the world into concepts and find an organizing principle for the chaos of them. It has served us well, this instinct to categorize in order to contain, giving us music, the laws of planetary motion, and democracy. Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/a-world-in-parts

The Journey (Peter Watkins, 1987). At Radio Canada, preparations are underway for Ronald Reagan’s 1985 summit with Canadian prime minister Brian Mulroney. Filmmaker Peter Watkins and his crew have been allowed into meetings where the broadcasters plan their coverage down to the second. Everyone must synchronize their watches: A discrepancy of 40 seconds, one participant warns, could throw off the day’s work. A shot requested at 17:02 might be missed if recorded 30 seconds later. “One thing is certain: there can’t be anything unexpected tonight,” another member of the team declares. Security officials will provide the presidential route, street by street, allowing the text to be prepared beforehand. “What you don’t have is the images.” Even the moment Reagan is scheduled to go behind the curtains to shake hands has been fixed: 9:03, already too late for the broadcasters’ purposes. Watkins’s voiceover draws our attention to the “constant emphasis on control and brevity.” What will later arrive in the viewer’s living room as news has, in one sense, already happened.

In this episode, the conversation explores Rodrigo Sorogoyen and Diego Luna’s earliest cinematic experiences and how trust and a sense of togetherness form the foundation of their approach to working with actors. Rodrigo Sorogoyen is a Spanish director and screenwriter whose work spans nearly twenty feature films, series and short films. His filmography moves between intricate narratives rooted in political and crime thrillers, and deeply intimate and socially driven dramas. His 2017 short film Madre was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film and later became the starting point for a 2019 feature-length adaptation, which premiered in the Orizzonti section of the Venice Film Festival. In 2022, he presented The Beasts at the Cannes Film Festival, earning the César Award for Best Foreign Film, Goya Awards for Best Director and Best Original Screenplay, and the San Sebastián Film Festival Audience Award. He also co-wrote and co-directed the romantic series The New Years (2024).

Attribution: MUBI Notebook [film_moving_image] https://mubi.com/en/notebook/posts/the-last-emperor-a-conversation-with-jeremy-thomas

The Last Emperor (Bernardo Bertolucci, 1987). When Jeremy Thomas died on September 11, 2026, the British film industry lost a titan. A producer who paid no heed to the vagaries of popular culture, Thomas was led by his impeccable palate for cinematic ambition, unswayed by whether audiences or critics came along for the ride. A list of filmmakers whose work makes up Thomas’s production portfolio reads like a who’s who of maverick visionaries, each of them fiercely loyal to the last: Nicolas Roeg and David Cronenberg; Takeshi Kitano and Jonathan Glazer; Nagisa Ōshima and Wim Wenders; Jerzy Skolimowski and Bernardo Bertolucci, whose The Last Emperor (1987) won Thomas the Academy Award for Best Picture. Cinema ran through Thomas’s veins. Both his father and uncle were filmmakers, respectively behind the uniquely British series of Doctor (1954–70) and Carry On (1958–92) films, and Thomas spent much of his youth on the sound stages at Pinewood Studios.

In this extract, taken from “The Myth And Mystery Of The New Blockaders”, Nick Soulsby outlines the unique biographical challenges in documenting the lives of North East refuseniks Richard and Philip Rupenus It’s common in biography for the sense of the person to become overwhelmed by their actions: the politician fades beneath crises and legislation; the general into a catalogue of battlefield decisions; the musician into the cycle of writing, recording and performing. Once set in motion, most lives worth writing of become dominated by a body of work with the human being whittled away to a delivery mechanism for its creation: “…A man takes a job and that job becomes what he is…You do a thing and that’s what you are…You get a job, you become the job,” as a character in Taxi Driver explains to Travis Bickle. In the case of The New Blockaders (TNB), to have the work stand on its own account was not, initially, extraordinary: so many artists leave interpretation to their audiences or keep a gap between work and life.

To accompany his Unlimited Editions report in The Wire 514, Tim Fish compiles an annotated playlist of tracks from the Liverpool label When Blah Records emerged into the UK’s hiphop landscape in 2006, they formed part of an alternative movement to a rather dominant London scene. Co-founded by Lee Scott and Alex Jennings (aka Molotov), the label was primarily a way to officially distribute music for the rap crew Children Of The Damned (COTD), and the majority of artists who have put out records on the label over the subsequent 20 years have all had some real-life connection to Scott. The following playlist outlines some of Blah's most significant records. Children Of The Damned “Cold Sag Run Marathon” From Brick Pelican (2009) Children Of The Damned were the original Blah artists and they still remain at the core of the label today, albeit with expanded numbers and a slightly different name. This track gives a flavour of their origins and an even better indicator of how much their sound has evolved.

Mark Korven’s scores for The Black Phone (2021) and Them (2021) destabilise hermetic soundworlds to convey psychological violence, writes Philip Brophy in his latest Secret History of Film Music column The contribution of Canadian composer Mark Korven to contemporary horror cinema is aligned with composers who sculpt their scores through tactile manipulation. His self-built Apprehension Engine, a hybrid guitar-percussion instrument, empowers distinctive acoustic control. Korven commissioned Toronto based guitar maker Tony Duggan-Smith to build the modest box incorporating tools and techniques favoured by Korven: a hurdy-gurdy for cranking, a spring reverb for metallic resonance, metal rods and wooden tongues for bowing (similar to the waterphone), and a stretched wire for E-bowing. Its abject sonics pepper Robert Eggers’s The Lighthouse (2019) with terse shudders and emotional spikes, and are also audible in Adam Schindler and Brian Netto’s Don’t Move (2024).

To accompany his Global Ear feature in The Wire 514, Simon Coates compiles an annotated playlist of tracks from the Sri Lankan city Situated on Colombo’s Vauxhall Street, Musicmatters sits at the centre of the Sri Lankan city's experimental music world. “A lot of my introduction to experimentation in music came through Musicmatters around 2010,” says bass player Uvindu Perera. “I was new to it then, but these people were already listening widely and sharing references.” Simultaneously a collective, a school (Perera now teaches there), a record label and home to the Sound Room performance space, Musicmatters offers both an alternative to exam-heavy Western music education and provides space for explorations in sound as art and experimentation. Many of the musicians in this playlist have links to the organisation. Isuru Kumarasinghe “Time #1” From Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies (Bandcamp) 2020 “Time #1” is taken from the 2020 album, Ekāgra: Sitting With Trees Under Skies, that formed the soundtrack to a video artwork Isuru Kumarasinghe made during the Covid lockdowns.

Watch an exclusive clip of Turkish improv band ZeN’s Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital concert from 1998 On 23 June 1998, Istanbul based experimental rock group ZeN performed at Bakırköy Psychiatric Hospital, following an invitation from two nurses who worked there. The musicians visited the hospital beforehand and decided to approach the performance with sensitivity to their audience while remaining true to their commitment to improvisation. At times, the lyrics seem to tell the story of the hospital and the concert itself, responding directly to the surroundings. The performance subsequently became one of the group’s most remarkable and cult recordings, released on cassette and CD in 1999 and reissued on vinyl in 2023. This exclusive edit with English subtitles is hosted by The Wire ahead of the release of a new documentary, ZeNistan, exploring the activities of ZeN throughout the 1990s.

Source meta: culture_magazine · commentary · R4 · P4 · culture_probe

Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: ArchDaily [architecture_urbanism] https://www.archdaily.com/1026978/jiujiang-ferry-cultural-complex-renovation-turtlehill-architecture-and-design

The abandoned ferry terminal along the Xijiang River in Jiujiang Town, Foshan, once served as a vital dock connecting the riverine islands. With the commissioning of a new terminal, this structure—imbued with memories of waterway transportation—gradually fell into disuse, leaving only a concrete skeleton and steps leading to a decaying pier. Situated at the intersection of a wetland park and a residential area, the site combines ecological sensitivity with community service potential. The design team faced the challenge of transforming this ruin into a multifunctional public space—integrating a bookstore, exhibition hall, café, cultural events, and art performances—within a footprint of less than 150 square meters, while responding to the climatic characteristics of the Pearl River Delta and the region's industrial cultural context.

Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 16 November 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02638-7 Big team science seeks to make research more inclusive, but the cost of recruiting representative samples can vary markedly across countries. This risks reinforcing the very inequalities these collaborations seek to address. Pooling resources and asking funders to contribute according to their financial capacity could help to overcome these inequalities.

Researchers have discovered a new subtype of depression that may affect nearly one in four people with severe, recurrent, or persistent depression. Known as "circadian depression," it is linked to the body's internal clock and is associated with night owl tendencies, excessive sleep, persistent exhaustion, and more severe symptoms. Traditional antidepressants often work less effectively for these individuals, potentially explaining why some people struggle to find relief.

by Ifeyinwa Lilian Ezenwosu, John Olajide Olawepo, Jane Nnedinma Ohaekweiro, Peter Ezeogo Ihere, Emeka John Aneke, Justus Uchenna Onu, Oluchukwu Perpetual Okeke, Olajide Odunayo Sobande Introduction Human Papilloma Virus (HPV)-attributable cancers disproportionately affect adolescent girls and young women living with HIV (AGYWLHIV) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet HPV vaccination coverage in this subpopulation remains suboptimal. This systematic review and meta-analysis estimated the pooled prevalence of HPV vaccination coverage among AGYWLHIV in LMICs. Methods A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Cumulative Index to Nursing and Allied Health Literature (CINAHL), and Web of Science for observational studies published between January 2014 and December 2025. A random-effects meta-analysis was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of HPV vaccination coverage. Subgroup analyses by age group and vaccine type were conducted, while HPV vaccination delivery platforms were summarised descriptively.

Algamili Among the various factors, corona discharge is recognized as one of the most threatening to degrade polymeric insulators. Over time, corona-induced deterioration has become a more dominant phenomenon in extra- and ultrahigh-voltage transmission lines. Therefore, this study investigates the aging effects on optimally balanced weight-percentage samples of high-temperature-vulcanized silicone rubber/ethylene-propylene-diene monomer (HTV-SR/EPDM) incorporating boron nitride (BN) and silicon carbide (SiC) fillers to identify the most desirable composition for resistance to degradation. The nano-sized fillers were loaded at 1, 3, and 5 wt.%. The test samples were subjected to an AC corona discharge for 72 h, utilizing a multi-needle high-voltage electrode and a plane-grounded electrode arrangement.

by Samson Shumba, Maureen Aongola, Deborah Tembo Background Zambia expanded HIV testing substantially during the 2010s, but testing strategies changed after 2018 with the shift to targeted testing and the COVID-19 pandemic. We examined trends in HIV testing among adolescent girls between 2007 and 2024, and whether changes reflected shifts in the characteristics of adolescent girls or in how those characteristics related to testing. Methods We pooled data on 11,717 girls aged 15–19 years from the 2007, 2013/14, 2018 and 2024 Zambia Demographic and Health Surveys. Outcomes were ever having been tested for HIV and having been tested in the past 12 months and received the result. We used survey-weighted logistic regression, interaction models to estimate subgroup-specific changes, and multivariate decomposition, with Fairlie decomposition as a sensitivity analysis, to separate compositional change from changes in effects. Results Ever-testing rose from 23.0% in 2007 to 60.9% in 2018, then fell to 49.3% in 2024 (adjusted change −11.4 percentage points, 95% CI −14.0 to −8.8).

by Tao Yuan, Tianhong Yang, Zhenqi Yang, Qianbai Zhao, Yong Zhao, Jinduo Li, Ke Luo, Yuan Gao The Fe3O4/SiO2 ratio is an important compositional factor affecting the mechanical behavior of magnetite ore like materials. In this study, uniaxial compression simulations were carried out using particle flow models with different Fe3O4/SiO2 ratios, and the simulated crack evolution and acoustic emission (AE) responses were interpreted together with SEM-EDS observations. The uniaxial compressive strength varies non monotonically with the Fe3O4/SiO2 ratio. As the ratio decreased from 3.00 to 1.00, the peak strength decreased from 131.64 MPa to 81.95 MPa. Further decreases in the ratio to 0.60 and 0.33 increased the peak strength to 146.45 MPa and 151.01 MPa, respectively. At Fe3O4/SiO2 = 1.00, the heterogeneous mineral interfaces appeared highly connected, and cracks preferentially initiated and coalesced along weak SiO2-Fe3O4 and Fe3O4-Al2O3 contacts, producing through going failure paths and the lowest strength.

by Rigmor C. Berg, Miroslav Kojic, Asgeir Johannessen, Vegard Skogen Hepatitis B virus (HBV) represents a significant global health burden, with approximately 14 million infected individuals in EU/EEA countries. The alarmingly low proportions diagnosed, linked to, engaged and retained in care underscore the necessity for further evidence on HBV care continuum dynamics, as emphasized in the new World Health Organisation guidelines for HBV. We conducted a scoping review to identify and describe research addressing modifiable barriers and facilitators related to the care continuum for people living with HBV infection in EU/EEA countries, Switzerland and the United Kingdom. We pre-specified our methods in a protocol, conducted the review in line with a methodological guide, searched six databases, selected eligible studies in duplicate, and summarized data descriptively. We included 24 studies, of which most were published after 2016 and were observational quantitative studies.

arXiv:2611.28021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We report an experimental characterization of the wavelength-shifting (WLS) absorption length of the EJ-160I fiber core material from Eljen Technology. Fiber-core samples of different thicknesses were employed, and the transmitted intensity of incident LED light was measured to extract the WLS absorption length at 405.7 nm. The resulting value, (0.823 +/- 0.038) mm, was used to normalize the WLS absorption length spectrum derived from the absorption spectrum of the core material. An independent measurement at 392.5 nm yielded a WLS absorption length of (1.404 +/- 0.074) mm, differing from the value predicted by the reconstructed WLS absorption length spectrum by 3.16%, corresponding to 0.43 sigma. The resulting spectrum was implemented as an optical input in a Geant4-based optical Monte Carlo simulation of the EJ-160I fiber to examine the role of the WLS absorption length in light output, light attenuation, and the emission spectrum.

Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28052

arXiv:2611.28052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collisionless shocks are of fundamental interest in astrophysics and space physics as important sources of energetic particles. Downstream of quasi-parallel shocks, high-speed jets (HSJs) and magnetic reconnection have been frequently observed, while it remains unclear how their coupling shapes structured regions for particle energization. We use two-dimensional full particle-in-cell simulations to investigate HSJ generation, thin current sheet formation, and associated electron energization downstream of a parallel shock. We find that portions of foreshock ULF waves with enhanced dynamic pressure interact with a self-reforming shock front and are transmitted downstream, forming HSJs, while neighboring low pressure portions evolve into cavities. At the leading edge of the HSJs, the unique bent magnetic topology carried by the compressed ULF waves produces bow waves and locally squeezes out thin current sheets.

arXiv:2611.28070v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant Schottky detectors provide non-destructive, single-ion-sensitive measurements of revolution frequencies and intensities of ion species stored in a heavy-ion storage ring. These high-\(Q\) cavities allow analysis of high-order harmonics of the revolution frequencies to magnify absolute frequency separations. Adjacent harmonic ranges can, however, overlap within the detector band, making frequency alone insufficient for determining the ion's mass-to-charge ratio $(m/q)$. We present a proof-of-concept for an automated harmonic de-overlapping method using spectral shapes in combined Schottky and Isochronous Mass Spectrometry. The empirical ansatz is that, for a fixed ion-optical setting, each peak, corresponding to a specific ion species with given $m/q$ ratio, has a characteristic profile that evolves smoothly with changing $m/q$. Occurrences of the same local structure at different harmonics should therefore retain almost identical shapes after frequency rescaling.

arXiv:2611.28071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I propose and evaluate by simulation a wide-field dome optical receiver (a field of view larger than a hemisphere) at 1550 nm for the acquisition of inter-satellite laser links. The detector is an InGaAs pixel hybrid of about 1 Mpixel with event-driven, time-stamped readout, inspired by the pixel detectors of high-energy physics. A pulsed beacon is detected by the coincidence of m hits in a sliding block of pixels, and the angle of arrival (AoA) is estimated by clustering and centroiding and handed to a narrow-field data channel. In a 550 km Earth constellation, with a 5 mrad beacon and a 10 mm aperture, detection takes 12 $\mu$s to 2 ms (up to 116 ms with the 6-9 mm that the optics allow), with a whole-frame false-alarm rate below 0.01/s, and the AoA error is 0.13-0.23 mrad. Cooling to about 233 K gives a service life above 5 years for fluences up to about $2\times10^{9}$ p/cm$^2$ per year. The receiver is also studied around the Moon and on the Earth-Moon link, where it works only between high orbits.

### Revisiting the Fermi Paradox: Does the Math Hold up?
Source: arXiv
Published: 2026-11-24 05:00 UTC
URL: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28075
Source meta: preprint · primary · R4 · P5 · signal
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:18 UTC

Fetch status: ok
Attribution: arXiv [academic_research] https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.28075

arXiv:2611.28075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we present a stochastic model to address the famous Fermi Paradox, i.e. the supposed contradiction between the abundance of intelligent life in the universe and the absence of any evidence of it. The model assumes that life can arise and evolve on habitable planets with a certain chance, and that we can detect life on other planets within a certain distance. The parameters of the model include the rates, at which life arises, evolves, vanishes, or advances to "Space Age", i.e. a stage where it gains the capability of interstellar communication. Given any numerical choice of these parameters, the model estimates a Contact Probability, i.e. the probability of having received a signal from an extraterrestrial civilization during the ongoing Space Age on Earth. Based on a critical probability threshold, the model can identify regions in the parameter space where Contact Probability is low, i.e. where the absence of contact is the expected outcome rather than a paradox.

Although Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's victory in Brazil's presidential election promises executive commitment to science, public health, and environmental protection, the political reality signals a serious governability crisis. The unprecedented conservative surge in the 2026 legislative elections created a deeply hostile Congress, leaving a divided nation in which evidence-based governance, public health systems, and ecological preservation face imminent institutional gridlock. This political split, reflected in the 51·79% to 48·21% election result,1 is heightened by memories of past anti-democratic actions following the 2022 election, including civilian encampments outside military installations, demands for military intervention, and the January 2023 storming of Brasília's democratic institutions.

### [Review] Irritable bowel syndrome and related disorders of gut–brain interaction
Source: The Lancet
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01500-X/fulltext?rss=yes
Source meta: journal · primary · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-10-29 23:30 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:18 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: The Lancet [academic_research] https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lancet/article/PIIS0140-6736(26)01500-X/fulltext?rss=yes

Irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea are disorders of gut–brain interaction, the symptoms of which include abnormal stool consistency or frequency accompanied by varying degrees of abdominal pain, discomfort, bloating, or distension. These conditions affect 20% of the global population with a relapsing and remitting course. Risk factors include female sex, younger age, a history of common mental disorders, and acute enteric infection. The pathophysiology of irritable bowel syndrome, chronic constipation, and functional diarrhoea remain incompletely understood, but are thought to be secondary to aberrant interactions throughout the gut–brain axis, resulting in disordered gut motility and visceral hypersensitivity.

We are consistently launching more and more stuff into space. As of now, space agencies track more than 30,000 objects larger than a softball, with an expected one million more bullet-sized pieces of debris orbiting Earth that are too small to spot from the ground.. Government agencies and private commercial entities are planning to have up to 100,000 active spacecraft in orbit by the early 2030s, turning some orbital shells into crowded highways. And according to a new paper, available in preprint on arXiv by Federico Toson, a researcher at the University of Padova in Italy, the math that regulatory agencies use to determine whether a satellite is “safe” in these highly congested spaces is fundamentally flawed.

This post From New Variant to New Species: Unraveling the Mystery of the Pasture Mealybug appeared first on Entomology Today - Brought to you by the Entomological Society of America. A tiny, wax-covered scale insect found damaging pasture grasses and sugarcane in North America and Australia has been challenging to simply identify. When the bug arrived in Florida earlier this year, taxonomists at the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services, working with the United States Department of Agriculture, acted quickly to analyze the insect's morphology and genetics, discovering that the pestiferous pasture mealybug spreading throughout the New World represents a new species, Heliococcus novovillei. It's a key first step in knowing how to respond to manage the new invasive pest. [Read more] The post From New Variant to New Species: Unraveling the Mystery of the Pasture Mealybug appeared first on Entomology Today.

AI agents can generate code at a scale that’s hard for humans to review line-by-line. PDD Kit helps ensure the code is doing what the developer intended by creating formal specifications and testing against them. It converts developer intent into a Verus specification, proves AI-generated code meets it for every input, and uses tests where proofs aren't practical. Developers review intent, not every line. "Arthur T Knackerbracket" writes: https://arstechnica.com/security/2026/11/a-leaky-ai-supply-chain-is-exposing-secret-user-data-at-an-alarming-rate/ Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today's AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers. These "AI routers," sometimes also known as "AI gateways," receive large numbers of prompts sent from AI app end users and route them to an available inference engine based on criteria such as the one charging the lowest price or being best suited for the given task.

GPT 6.2 Astra Solves a Historical Mystery Here's an interesting case-study in using GPT-6.2 Astra for historical research, from history professor Mark Humphries: With only minimal prompting, GPT-6.2 Astra was able to autonomously identify the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook held at Yale’s Beinecke Library. It did so extremely quickly (in just 22 minutes), using publicly available primary and secondary sources. To do so, it discovered a little known source in a paper archive, predicted that it would prove its hypothesis if examined and, in the end, it did. Not only that, but this new source turns out to be a major find on its own that will be of significant interest to both Canadian and fur trade historians. Here's the digitized sketchbook. Astra found a diary reference reference to a visit by the vicomte de Chabot dated five days before a date mentioned in the sketchbook at a nearby river, and suggested that Chabot's journal of his travels (only available by order from Cleveland State University) might confirm that the sketchbook was his work.

"Arthur T Knackerbracket" writes: https://www.cnet.com/tech/hackers-artex-ai-cyberattacks-fbi-warning/ An open-source AI tool designed to find security flaws is helping hackers launch cyberattacks. The FBI says hackers are using Artex, an AI-powered security testing tool, to break into organizations worldwide. In an advisory on Friday [PDF], the agency said some attacks took less than 3 hours from selecting a target to gaining high-level access to its systems. Attackers have used Artex since at least August against banks, government agencies, technology companies and healthcare providers. The advisory was issued the same day communications problems prompted a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration ground stop and a day after a major Microsoft 365 outage began. Microsoft attributed its disruption to technical problems, and the FAA says it has found no indication of a cyberattack. An FBI official told ABC News⁠ that Artex doesn’t appear to be connected to either incident or to other recent disruptions, including banking outages involving JPMorgan Chase.

hubie writes: Research finds that 17th Century trader exhibited modern toxic leadership traits: New research suggests the same personality traits associated with toxic corporate leaders today may have been present at the very birth of global capitalism 400 years ago. The study, published in the Asian Journal of Business Ethics identifies Jeronimus Cornelisz, who was a merchant manager with the Dutch East India Company, as likely being the earliest documented example of a corporate psychopath. The research, by Dr Clive Boddy of Anglia Ruskin University (ARU), is believed to be the first to systematically assess Cornelisz's behaviour using a recognised corporate psychopathy framework rather than relying solely on historical interpretation. The study found that he displayed all 10 of the core characteristics associated with corporate psychopaths.

GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. GLM 5.4 is not yet available as open weights: We plan to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening. I tried it out using the Z.

Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS. This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha, which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself! I've been trying it out today, and it's very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I've tried to load in it have worked as they should.

Marcus Borg recounts an experiment to investigate if healthy code was cheaper for agents to review. Between a typical unhealthy pull request (CodeHealth 2.8) and a typical healthy one (9.7), that adds up to 22 to 35%. The measures of health come from CodeScene. The experiment looked at three LLMs, 465 pull requests on 246 open source repositories. Each pull request was put through a review and fix pipeline involving five agents. Data contracts are a way to describe the contents and guarantees of datasets. Simon Harrer and Arif Wider describe in detail what they are and how to use them. They apply practices from API design to data by treating them as data-providing services - such as data products - whose interfaces we want to define as clearly as possible. This approach significantly increases the robustness of large-scale data landscapes, and gives both people and AI agents the explicit, trustworthy metadata they need to work with data autonomously, which is why more and more enterprises are adopting them. more…

### Deterministic Simulation Testing
Source: Martin Fowler
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://martinfowler.com/articles/deterministic-simulation-testing.html
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-17 14:33 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:19 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/articles/deterministic-simulation-testing.html

Distributed systems are hard to test because partial failures overlap with live traffic and the same fault can produce different execution traces on different runs. Unmesh Joshi describes how deterministic simulation testing addresses this by replacing real clocks, networks, and storage with simulated components driven by a single-threaded execution loop. This allows simulating both hard failures and routine slowdowns—such as network and disk latency spikes—and more importantly makes every execution reproducible. This article explains the technique using a quorum key-value store as a running example, with code from Tickloom, a Java implementation of the approach. more…

### Bliki: Generated Glossary
Source: Martin Fowler
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-12 14:15 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:19 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/bliki/GeneratedGlossary.html

When we use LLMs in a specialized domain, such as the operations of any reasonably-large organization, there is a lot of specialized vocabulary. Such words and specialized meanings will be foreign to an LLM because they aren't in its training set, making it harder for the LLM to be effective when doing tasks in that domain. One technique to aid this is to use an LLM to generate a glossary of the terminology in that domain, and make this glossary available for any LLMs doing work in those circumstances. The sources for the LLM can be any material within the organization concerned such as documents, emails, and chat logs. In some cases getting transcripts of audio or video may be helpful, although most organizations generate enough text to do the job. The glossary-generating LLM should look for single words, and phrases of several words that regularly hang out together to form a meaningful term. The generator should be asked to identify terms that are new to it, but also known terms that are being used in unfamiliar ways. The latter can often cause the most confusion.

### Tests as data: ensuring AI-generated code does what we want
Source: Martin Fowler
Published: Publication date unknown / 发布日期未知
URL: https://martinfowler.com/articles/tests-as-data.html
Source meta: specialist_media · specialist · R5 · P5 · baseline
Updated: 2026-11-11 15:17 UTC
Fetched: 2026-11-25 03:19 UTC
Review: R/P: legacy rating, evidence review pending / 历史评分，依据待复核
Fetch status: ok
Attribution: Martin Fowler [computing_cultures] https://martinfowler.com/articles/tests-as-data.html

Automated testing in the age of AI coding assistants is problematic: when AI agents write both production and test code, developers risk losing the assurance that automated tests protect against functional errors. Matteo Vaccari makes three claims: (1) when AI writes the code, developers become its customers; (2) therefore customer tests, not developer tests, become the primary contract between humans and AI; (3) moving that contract into test data rather than test code makes it easier to protect it from unexpected modifications by coding agents. All of this optimizes for human-readable tests that establish a contract between humans and AI. While in the past DSL parsers and custom test runners were expensive to write and maintain, now AI makes them cheap. more…

It’s that time of the year when the November Thoughtworks Technology Radar appears. Again my colleagues have taken a sweep of the technologies that our teams have used in the field, and pulled together a summary of what’s popped up in the last six months. It’s been a busy half-year, one that again has been dominated by AI, and that’s reflected in the many AI blips on the radar. The mass of blips makes it hard to develop a coherent story around trends, but Chris Ford has done a fine job of the writing the accompanying article on macro trends. One team of passionate people experimenting with agents can make almost anything work. They share a context, a credit card and a mental model. They review each other’s work because they sit together, and they know what to check and how much latitude to give the coding agent. Two hundred people, though, cannot work that way. The moment agentic AI becomes an operating model rather than a pilot, a second layer of problems appears: How is context shared between teams? What’s the token bill? How do we deal with increased review demands?

Legacy runtimes, such as node22, now use the open-source images in the vercel/sandbox repository, distributed through Vercel Container Registry (VCR). Sandboxes created with these now come with 64 GB of storage and use the same infrastructure as sandboxes powered by VCR. The universal image is released nightly, and rolling tags such as latest pick up operating system, dependency, and coding agent updates. Pin an image digest when you need a reproducible environment. Sandboxes created with version 3 or later of the JavaScript Sandbox SDK use vercel/sandbox/universal:latest by default. For over 20 years, we have protected 4 billion users and 13 million organizations in Workspace, and critical enterprise and government systems on Google Cloud. From personal and financial records to board materials, regulated workloads, applications, and AI models, those safeguards protect what matters most. Blocking >99.9% of spam, phishing, and malware, alongside encryption and data residency, follows one principle: your data is yours, and you should always know and decide who can access it. That trust has powered one of the world’s largest developer ecosystems. Workspace APIs now handle more than 2.8 trillion calls a month, and public Google Drive API traffic alone is more than two-and-a-half times the volume of 2022. More than 18 billion reads from Drive each day come from API callers. Traditional REST APIs were built for human-paced apps where a valid OAuth token implied user intent. As AI agents shift from reading information to acting autonomously at machine speed across email, documents, datasets, and cloud infrastructure, a valid token is no longer enough.

Enterprise teams using Secure Compute can now create and manage AWS PrivateLink endpoints directly from the Vercel dashboard. Endpoints on Secure Compute live in your team's dedicated VPC and use the network's AWS region. They belong to the network and are shared by its connected project environments. Vercel Functions, Vercel Sandbox, and builds connected to the network can reach AWS-hosted backends over the AWS private network. Before you add an endpoint in Vercel, the backend must already be exposed through a published AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. Examples include RDS, Aurora, Redshift, Snowflake, MongoDB Atlas, and internal services behind a Network Load Balancer. In Team Settings → Networking, open your Secure Compute network and choose Add Endpoint from the PrivateLink tab. Standard pricing for new endpoints: Each Secure Compute network includes one AWS PrivateLink endpoint. Additional endpoints cost $30 per month each. PrivateLink data transfer costs $0.04 per GB. With flags@4.5.0, projects on Vercel can use Flags Explorer and precompute without FLAGS_SECRET. That cuts out a setup step for new projects and removes the need to keep a shared secret in sync across microfrontends. Vercel signs Flags Explorer discovery requests and overrides, and the SDK encrypts flag values shown in the Vercel Toolbar with Vercel’s public key. Existing projects keep using FLAGS_SECRET while the environment variable is set or the secret is passed in code. Upgrading alone doesn't switch them to Vercel-managed keys. To use Vercel-managed keys for these features, remove the environment variable and any code that passes the secret explicitly. For local development, run vercel env pull. Precomputed codes created without a secret work only in the deployment that created them. Precompute without a secret requires Vercel system environment variables, which are enabled by default. Prebuilt deployments and codes that must work across deployments still need a secret; use FLAGS_PRECOMPUTE_SECRET if only precompute needs one.

This feature gives you the ability to quickly meet compliance and security requirements when sensitive data needs to be purged from run payloads. Deleting a run's data deletes any inputs, outputs, hook payloads, and error traces for the run and its related entities. This does not delete the run's metadata: the run is still listed in observability. Attributes, hook tokens, and timings for steps and events can still be inspected. You can delete a run's data from the Vercel Dashboard, or via the CLI: You can also delete a run's data programmatically from your code: Deletion applies to finished runs only, so a run that is still going is skipped and keeps running. If you want to delete a run's payload as soon as it finishes, use the retention settings instead. Upgrade to workflow@5.7.0 or higher to use this feature. Learn more in the deleteRuns() reference. Read more

Open models like Gemma 4 from Google DeepMind are a great option to keep your data local. But how can a local AI model integrate with on-premises data? With AlloyDB Omni, you can build agentic experiences on your own infrastructure and on your own terms. Whether it’s in the cloud, in your datacenter, or even on your laptop, you can have data plus AI anywhere. Built-in AI for your local environment AlloyDB Omni is a downloadable, run-anywhere edition of AlloyDB that easily deploys to your own infrastructure, including on-premises. AlloyDB Omni packs powerful, built-in AI, including the same ScaNN indexing technology powering Google Search. When you pair AlloyDB Omni with a model, you can store vector embeddings at scale; search them semantically; and even query the database using natural language. You can use virtually any model you like, whether that’s a frontier Cloud-hosted model like Gemini or a local model.

As the scale of global communications grows larger and larger, enterprise platforms must process billions of interactions with customers across a complex network of touchpoints without breaking them. A prime example is Sinch, one of the world’s leading cloud communications and customer engagement (CPaaS) companies, which processes billions of customer interactions, SMS routing events, voice calls, and transactional messages. Managing massive international messaging traffic brings significant architectural challenges, so Sinch built a distributed, multi-cloud data footprint across AWS and GCP, with separate Snowflake instances running in the EU, US, and Australia. To eliminate data silos, curb monthly billing spikes, establish a single governed source of truth, and unlock the next generation of predictive AI capabilities, Sinch partnered with Google Cloud Professional Services to migrate its enterprise data warehouse to Google BigQuery.

The information listed below is based on the current status of the v1.38 release and may change before the actual release date. Deprecations and removals for Kubernetes v1.38 kubectl: WebSocket opt-out environment variables removed kubectl has used WebSockets instead of SPDY by default for kubectl exec, attach and cp since v1.30, and for kubectl port-forward since v1.31.
